To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
leptin is a hormone which plays an important part in the regulation of body weight.
the high-fat phenotype is associated with higher concentrations of plasma fasting leptin.
leptin concentrations are significantly higher in HF consumers than in LF consumers and this difference is independent of BMI and % BF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physiological mechanisms which could influence the energy balance of habitual high-fat (high energy) consumers.
the physiological and biochemical responses of the human body to the consumption of high-fat diets.
the relationship between dietary fat and leptin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HF and LF consumers do differ in concentrations of fasting leptin.
HF consumers are not necessarily overweight and that leptin may be involved in the adaptation of the human body to a high fat diet.
the HF phenotype is associated with a higher plasma leptin concentration and a lower glucose concentration, but not necessarily with higher body weight.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the high-fat phenotype is associated with a lower energy expenditure, which is compensated by a higher energy intake.
leptin is a good predictor of body fatness and may be involved in the adaptive mechanism which prevents the development of obesity in HF consumers.
leptin is involved in the adaptive responses to a high fat diet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the high-fat phenotype is not just a matter of eating more calories, but also a matter of how your body adapts to that high-fat diet.
leptin is a good biomarker of the fat content of the diet, and can be used to monitor changes in dietary fat content.
the body has a mechanism that helps to prevent weight gain in the face of high fat diets, and that this mechanism involves a hormone called leptin.
